name: pkill
description: Sends signals to processes selected by name, pattern, or attributes — pkill NAME is the shortcut for kill $(pgrep NAME).

flags.description: Signal matching processes with SIGTERM (15) by default.
-KILL: force kill (cannot be caught or cleaned up).
Send SIGHUP — many daemons reload their configuration on it.
Exact match of the whole name.

examples.explanation: Politely asks all chrome processes to terminate (SIGTERM).
Force-kills the matching script. -9 is a last resort — processes get no chance to save state.
Reloads nginx worker processes without dropping connections — the classic graceful reload signal.

about: Signals: SIGTERM (15) requests a clean shutdown; SIGKILL (9) is immediate and unconditional; SIGHUP (1) conventionally means "reload config"; SIGSTOP/SIGCONT pause and resume. Always try SIGTERM first.
useCases: Kill all processes of a pattern at once.
mistakes: Starting with -9 out of habit — it prevents programs from flushing data and removing lock files.
Matching too broadly: pkill ssh can kill your own session's sshd child.
warnings: pkill -9 -f with a loose pattern can match your own shell command line and kill your session. Verify with pgrep -a first.
